cards.title: China confirms Xi will host Trump and Putin on 19 November
cards.summary: China's foreign ministry said Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads-of-state meeting with Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November, the first such summit. It named world peace and strategic stability as topics. The White House had announced the meeting on 14 November with nuclear-arms cuts and the Iran war on its agenda.
cards.body:
All three governments have now put the Shenzhen meeting on the record. On 16 November China's foreign ministry said Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads-of-state meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump on 19 November, without giving an agenda in its first statement (Japan Times). Spokeswoman Mao Ning later said the leaders would hold 'in-depth exchanges' on world peace and strategic stability in major-power relations (France 24). The White House had announced the meeting on 14 November, saying Trump wants to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals and the war with Iran, and that Ukraine is not expected to be on the agenda (BBC; Al Jazeera). The Kremlin had also confirmed it.

The stated agendas differ: Washington frames the meeting around arms reductions, while Beijing speaks of strategic stability. No binding US-Russia limit on strategic forces has been in force since New START expired in February.

The meeting falls in a crowded week. ASEAN and China failed again to conclude a South China Sea code of conduct, with the Philippines saying about 80% of the text is agreed (Al Jazeera). NATO has dropped its planned 2027 leaders' summit in Albania and is cutting ministerial meetings (Kyiv Post, citing AP), while Lithuania has asked Washington for a permanent base (LRT).

Assessment (inference): a scheduled summit is engagement, not a change in posture, so the great-power axis stays at 70 until content emerges. The test is whether Shenzhen produces anything written on nuclear arms or Iran, or only a photograph. Watch for a joint statement, a separate Trump-Xi meeting, and how Moscow and Beijing describe the outcome.

cards.confidenceNote: Estonia from ERR News (prosecutor and security service statements, 15-16 Nov); EU boarding from Kallas via Kyiv Independent; Israel case from Shin Bet via Times of Israel; Megaspeed from BBC.
cards.title: Estonia blames Russia's GRU for arson attempt at a drone maker
cards.summary: Estonia detained eight Latvian residents after an arson attempt at drone maker Threod Systems on 14 November and its security service blamed Russia's GRU. It says about 10 Estonian defence firms are targeted and plans to close three crossings with Russia. An EU naval force boarded a false-flagged tanker on 13 November.
cards.body:
The hybrid campaign against Europe's defence industry produced its clearest state attribution and its strongest response this week. Estonia's prosecutor and Internal Security Service said an attempt to break into Threod Systems' site near Tallinn and set a fire at 03:06 on 14 November was stopped by the company's own security; eight residents of Latvia were detained and prosecutors sought arrest for five (ERR News). The security service chief attributed the operation to Russia's GRU, said it had advance intelligence, and said Russia is targeting around 10 Estonian defence companies. It is the second such attack since August, after one on Milrem Robotics. The government says road crossings at Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa will close on 1 December, pending cabinet discussion; Russia's foreign ministry called it 'Russophobia' (ERR News).

At sea, an EU naval force boarded the crude tanker MIDAG in the Mediterranean on 13 November and found it sailing under a false flag, Kaja Kallas said; it is the second such boarding after the Sun in August (Kyiv Independent).

Other cases ran in parallel. Israel's Shin Bet said an Israeli man will be charged with spying for Iran after sending coordinates of military bases (Times of Israel). In the Nvidia affair, the Singapore firm Megaspeed said the woman at the centre of the spying allegation left its executive team in 2025 (BBC); no government has charged her. Britain's case against the US Army member arrested near Gloucester has not yet produced a charge.

Assessment (inference): naming the GRU on the record and closing a border is a step beyond arrests, and it is the trigger this board watches for allied threat responses. Watch for Estonia's cabinet decision, a Russian countermeasure, and whether other Baltic states follow.

cards.confidenceNote: Bahrain interception from Bahrain's military via BBC; carrier from a US official to ABC News via Iran International; tanker from UKMTO via Arab News; Trump's restraint from Reuters via Iran International.
cards.title: Bahrain intercepts Iranian drones as a third US carrier arrives
cards.summary: Bahrain's military said it intercepted Iranian drones aimed at a US base on 15 November, two days after US forces downed two others. The carrier Theodore Roosevelt entered the region the same day, the third there. UKMTO said a tanker leaving Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile on 16 November.
cards.body:
Iran has now fired at Bahrain twice in three days, and the second attack is on the record from Bahrain itself. On 15 November Bahrain's military said its air defences intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones 'before they could achieve their objectives', and its foreign ministry condemned the attacks (BBC). The Guard said it sent six drones at a US air-defence radar at Riffa air base and declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. On 13 November US forces had shot down two Guard drones aimed at Bahrain, with no damage, according to the US military.

The US added force rather than striking back. The carrier Theodore Roosevelt entered Central Command's area on 15 November, joining the George H.W. Bush and George Washington, a US official told ABC News (Iran International). Reuters reported that Trump is considering holding off on new strikes unless Iran or the Houthis provoke the US, after Saudi Arabia's crown prince and Turkey's president urged restraint. The US has confirmed no new strike on Iran since 6 November; Iranian media reported an unattributed strike at Sirik on 12 November.

At sea, UKMTO said a tanker leaving the Gulf was hit by an unknown projectile on 16 November, starting an engine-room fire with no injuries (Arab News). The Guard separately claims two tankers hit mines and that a loaded supertanker sank; no maritime authority has confirmed either claim. In Yemen, government forces withdrew from the Bab al-Mandab area to defend Aden, and Houthi media say the group has retaken it (BBC).

Assessment (inference): direct Iranian fire at a US host state plus a three-carrier force raises the chance of a renewed exchange, but no major power is fighting another, so the kinetic axis stays at 75, inside the band for a formal blockade and multiple disrupted chokepoints. The Guard's claim to have closed the Strait again comes with no published zone. Watch for a US strike, any damage report from Riffa, and the shooter in the 16 November tanker attack.

cards.confidenceNote: Trump's Truth Social post and Vance instruction via Iran International (12 Nov) and BBC; restraint report from Reuters via Iran International; Pakistan and ECO via The New Arab.
cards.title: Trump pulls Vance off Iran talks, saying no deal is needed
cards.summary: Trump told Vice-President Vance on 12 November to stop working on Iran talks, writing 'We don't need a deal with Iran'. No US delegation joined talks by 15 November. Reuters reported Trump may hold off on strikes unless provoked, and Pakistan says it will keep mediating.
cards.body:
The diplomatic track lost its American lead this week. On 12 November Trump wrote on Truth Social that 'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,' and told JD Vance, who had been leading efforts to restart negotiations, to devote his attention to domestic politics (Iran International; BBC). The Wall Street Journal reported, citing two officials, that Trump privately regards the June memorandum Vance helped negotiate as a mistake that let Iran regroup. Trump said Iran's regime 'is collapsing' and that he would use force without hesitation to protect allies and shipping.

No US delegation joined talks with Iran before 15 November. Qatar's mediation continues without a timetable, and Iran repeats its conditions for reopening the Strait, including lifting the blockade and releasing frozen assets. Reuters reported on 14 November that Trump is considering holding off on strikes unless Iran or the Houthis carry out new provocations, after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkey's Erdogan urged restraint (Iran International). Two days of Guard fire at Bahrain followed. On 16 November Pakistan's foreign minister said Islamabad would keep working to ease US-Iran tensions with regional states at an Economic Cooperation Organisation meeting attended by Iran's foreign minister (The New Arab).

Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's economy could shrink by a quarter within a year (Iran International).

Assessment (inference): with the US saying it does not need an agreement, a negotiated reopening of Hormuz before the end of November looks less likely, and the blockade is the policy. Mediation now runs through Qatar, Pakistan and Turkey rather than Washington. Watch whether Trump raises Iran with Xi and Putin on 19 November, and any new US envoy.

cards.confidenceNote: Mandate from The Guardian and the NYT (7 Nov); Eisenkot statement and Channel 12 report via France 24 (16 Nov); spy case from Shin Bet via Times of Israel.
cards.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu 'cannot remain' over alleged election meddling
cards.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate to form Israel's government, said caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu 'cannot remain' after a report that Netanyahu's chief of staff steered police toward a pre-election complaint against an Arab party. The two camps had discussed a unity government hours earlier. Eisenkot's mandate runs to early December.
cards.body:
Israel's coalition talks turned sharper on 15 November. Hours after representatives of Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot discussed a possible national unity government, Eisenkot said Netanyahu 'cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer' and called his conduct a direct threat to democracy (France 24). He was reacting to a Channel 12 report that on the eve of the election Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, phoned the police commissioner's office with a complaint about members of the Arab party Ra'am and pointed officers to a source who had worked in Netanyahu's office.

The numbers have not changed. President Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate on 7 November after more lawmakers recommended him than Netanyahu; he has 28 days, extendable by 14 (The Guardian; New York Times). The 27 October election left Netanyahu's bloc with 53 of 120 seats and Eisenkot's camp 48, so a majority needs either ultra-Orthodox parties or Arab-backed support, or a deal with Likud.

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister with authority over military operations, including Iran and Lebanon. Mossad chief Roman Gofman has returned from talks with senior US officials in Washington (Iran International). Separately, the Shin Bet said an Israeli man will be charged with spying for Iran after sending coordinates of military bases (Times of Israel).

Assessment (inference): the longer the caretaker period runs, the longer Iran decisions rest with a prime minister fighting for his position, which is a risk for the Iran front rather than a settled fact. Watch for unity-talk outcomes, the police inquiry, and any Israeli action against Iran or Hezbollah during the mandate.

cards.confidenceNote: Bahrain from BBC; carrier from Iran International citing ABC News; Estonia from ERR News; China's summit date from Japan Times and France 24; Bab al-Mandab from BBC.
cards.title: Iran fires at Bahrain as China confirms the three-way summit
cards.summary: Bahrain intercepted Iranian drones aimed at a US base on 15 November and a third US carrier arrived. China confirmed Xi will host Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November. Estonia blamed Russia's GRU for arson at a drone maker, and the Houthis say they retook the Bab al-Mandab area.
cards.body:
The week's pressure points sit in three places, and none has yet changed the headline.

In the Gulf, Iran fired at Bahrain twice in three days; Bahrain's military intercepted the 15 November drones and its foreign ministry condemned the attack (BBC). The US answered with posture, not strikes: a third carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, entered the region (Iran International, citing ABC News), while Trump reportedly weighs holding off unless provoked and has said Washington does not need a deal. A tanker leaving Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile on 16 November, and in Yemen government forces fell back on Aden from the Bab al-Mandab area, which the Houthis say they have retaken (BBC).

In Europe, Russia's hybrid campaign met a harder response. Estonia named the GRU for an arson attempt at a drone maker and plans to close its main road crossings with Russia on 1 December (ERR News); the EU boarded a false-flagged tanker; Lithuania asked for a permanent US base. Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge and an airfield deep in Russia.

In great-power diplomacy, China confirmed it will host the first Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on 19 November (Japan Times), with Washington seeking nuclear cuts and Beijing speaking of 'strategic stability'.

Assessment (inference): the third carrier is posture inside the great-power band, not the direct major-power involvement the next band needs, so the four sub-axes stay at kinetic 75, great-power 70, WMD 60 and alliance 60, for a headline of 66. Kinetic would need direct fighting between major powers to reach 80; great-power moves on what the summit produces, not on its scheduling; alliance would need allies pulling out of a joint operation. The likeliest near-term movers are a US strike on Iran after the Bahrain attacks, or a written nuclear outcome in Shenzhen.

cards.confidenceNote: Talks outcome from The Guardian, France 24, Al Jazeera and NPR; Kyiv strike counts from the Ukrainian Air Force via Kyiv Independent; Moldova from Moldovan authorities via Kyiv Independent. Europe negotiators from Al Jazeera and The Moscow Times; Gulf of Finland from BBC and Defense News; Bild terms via LRT and Politico.
cards.title: Europe names Ukraine negotiators after Abu Dhabi prisoner deal
cards.summary: After Abu Dhabi produced the war's largest prisoner exchange, EU leaders named five countries to represent Europe in future talks; the Kremlin says Europe must first show readiness. Ukraine says it hit a Russian corvette in the Gulf of Finland, and drones struck three ships off Romania.
cards.body:
The first US-mediated talks in nine months ended on 11 November with one deliverable and one unresolved core. The deliverable is a prisoner exchange that Kushner said would involve more than 1,000 people from each side, the largest of the war. Ukraine's David Arakhamia reported 'really big progress' on post-war security guarantees and spoke of momentum toward a solution before the new year. The core is territory: Russia's team came with what Arakhamia called very strict directives, Moscow still demands the rest of Donetsk and all of Donbas, and Zelensky rules out concessions.

The format is widening. After Putin met Witkoff and Kushner on 12 November, EU leaders named France, Germany, Italy, Poland and Britain as Europe's negotiators, and US envoys say Putin agreed to European participation; Peskov says Europe must first show readiness to contribute (Al Jazeera; The Moscow Times). Bild reports unofficial Russian terms that reach NATO basing in the Baltics and Finland's membership; Finland's defence minister rejected the demand (Politico). The White House has set a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC next week.

The fighting did not pause. On 11 November Russia launched a Kh-59/69 missile, 163 drones and Banderol cruise missiles; two Banderols crossed Moldova's airspace for several minutes, and strikes killed nine people across Ukraine that day. Hours after the talks closed, Russia struck Kyiv with an Iskander-M and 123 drones, killing one person. Ukraine attacked Omsk, home to Russia's largest refinery, for more than eight hours, and hit Ust-Luga, where Estonia's defence minister said a Baltic Fleet vessel was damaged. Drones on the Ust-Luga route strayed over Lithuania and Estonia, and NATO jets failed to bring one down. Rosneft has capped fuel sales in at least four Russian regions. On 11 November Finland detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine says was the corvette Naro-Fominsk, and on 13-14 November drones hit three ships off Romania.

Assessment (inference): the prisoner deal builds trust but does not close the territorial gap that has blocked every round. The next markers are Putin's reply to the envoys, the timing of the exchange, and whether either side offers a limited energy or maritime ceasefire. Neither side has announced one. A failure in Moscow would likely bring a heavier Russian strike; Ukraine's long-range campaign on refineries looks set to continue regardless.

iran_lead.title: Bahrain confirms Iranian drone attack as third US carrier arrives
iran_lead.summary: Bahrain's military said it intercepted Iranian drones aimed at a US base on 15 November, Iran's second attack there in three days. A third US aircraft carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, entered the region the same day. A tanker leaving Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile on 16 November.
facts: 15 November: Bahrain's military said its air defences intercepted Iranian drones; the Guard said it fired six at a US radar at Riffa air base and called the Strait closed (BBC).
15 November: the USS Theodore Roosevelt entered Central Command's area, joining two other carriers, a US official told ABC News (Iran International).
16 November: UKMTO said a tanker leaving the Gulf was hit by an unknown projectile, starting an engine-room fire; no injuries (Arab News).
12 November: Trump told Vance to stop working on Iran talks, writing 'We don't need a deal with Iran' (Iran International; BBC).
14 November: Reuters reported Trump is considering holding off on strikes unless Iran or the Houthis provoke the US (Iran International).
15 November: Yemen's Saudi-backed forces withdrew from the Bab al-Mandab area to defend Aden; Houthi media say the group retook it (BBC).
iran_lead.changed: Iran's 15 November attack on Bahrain moved from a Guard claim to a Bahraini statement: its air defences intercepted the drones, and its foreign ministry condemned the attack. The US added a third carrier while Trump reportedly weighs holding off on strikes unless provoked, and he has said Washington no longer needs a deal. A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait. In Yemen, government forces withdrew from the Bab al-Mandab area, which the Houthis say they have retaken.
iran_lead.watch: Whether the US answers the Bahrain attacks with strikes on Iran; any US statement on damage at Riffa; who fired at the tanker on 16 November; Houthi moves toward Aden and shipping in Bab al-Mandab; the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on 19 November, where the Iran war is on the US agenda.

brics_lead.title: China confirms Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen on 19 November
brics_lead.summary: China's foreign ministry said Xi Jinping will host Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November, confirming the first three-way summit; it said talks will cover world peace and strategic stability. ASEAN and China again failed to agree a South China Sea code. NATO will hold no leaders' summit in 2027.
brics_lead.changed: All three governments have now announced the Shenzhen meeting, with China naming the date and a 'strategic stability' agenda while the US wants nuclear-arms cuts and the Iran war discussed. Around it, ASEAN and China missed a deal on a South China Sea code, and NATO trimmed its meeting calendar, dropping a 2027 leaders' summit. Lithuania asked for a permanent US base.
brics_lead.watch: Whether the 19 November meeting yields any nuclear or Iran statement; a Trump-Xi bilateral; the Quad summit date in Manila; the White House decision on permanent troops in Poland; North Korean launches.

facts: 16 November: China's foreign ministry said Xi will hold a China-Russia-US heads-of-state meeting with Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November (Japan Times).
16 November: spokeswoman Mao Ning said the leaders will discuss world peace and strategic stability (France 24).
16 November: ASEAN and China failed to conclude a South China Sea code of conduct; about 80% of the draft is agreed (Al Jazeera).
12 November: Albania's prime minister confirmed NATO's 2027 leaders' summit is off; NATO is cutting ministerial meetings (Kyiv Post).
16 November: Lithuania handed the US proposals for a permanent US base (LRT).
14 November: the White House said Trump will meet Xi and Putin at APEC, with nuclear-arms cuts on the agenda (BBC; Al Jazeera).

ukraine_lead.title: Estonia blames Russia for drone-maker arson and moves to shut border
ukraine_lead.summary: Estonia detained eight people after a thwarted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems and blamed Russia's military intelligence; it plans to close three road crossings with Russia from 1 December. Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge overnight into 16 November, forcing its closure. An EU naval force boarded a false-flagged tanker.
facts: 14 November: an arson attempt at Threod Systems was thwarted; eight Latvian residents detained; the security service named the GRU and says about 10 defence firms are targeted (ERR News).
15-16 November: Estonia's foreign minister said crossings at Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa would shut on 1 December, pending cabinet; Moscow called it 'Russophobia' (ERR News).
16 November: Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge, forcing its closure; Russia claimed it downed 1,336 drones (Kyiv Post).
15 November: Ukraine struck Akhtubinsk airfield, about 650 km from the front (Kyiv Post).
13 November: an EU naval force boarded the false-flagged tanker MIDAG in the Mediterranean, Kallas said (Kyiv Independent).
15 November: Russia launched 132 drones in a mass attack on Odesa region; four killed and 69 injured across Ukraine over the day (Kyiv Independent).
16 November: Lithuania handed the US proposals for a permanent US base (LRT).
ukraine_lead.changed: Russia's pressure on Europe's home front drew the sharpest answer yet: Estonia named the GRU for an arson attempt on a drone maker and plans to close its main road crossings with Russia. The EU boarded a second false-flagged tanker, and Lithuania asked for a permanent US base. On the battlefield Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge and an airfield deep in Russia, while Russian drones hit Odesa region. Britain's prime minister rejected reported Russian demands over its nuclear deterrent.
ukraine_lead.watch: Estonia's cabinet decision on the crossings and any Russian countermeasure; the start of the agreed prisoner exchange; EU ministers' adoption of new listings; whether Europeans join a negotiating session; damage to the Crimean Bridge; another mass missile attack.
